thread:
alex: we saw a spike where primary model queue filled and requests fell back straight to the tiny fallback, skipping the mid-tier reduced-context model. need to change routing order and header precedence.

maria: yep noticed it in the dashboard at ~09:12, p95 latency for /v1/generate shot up then cb opened.

chris: current policy evaluates by route matcher -> tenant header -> lane priority. seems header precedence can get clobbered by the gateway rewrite.

sam: cb trigger was error_rate>0.12 OR latency_p95>2s per policy. in this case latency triggered then cb stayed open for 30s and routing path collapsed to backup-small.

alex: proposal: explicit fallback chain list on the route config. e.g. fallback_chain: [primary, reduced-context, compressed-context, backup-small] and a header X-RI-Fallback-Priority to allow tenant-specified soft-preference. header should be advisory not override.

maria: SGTM but need to keep tenant isolation — header cannot force bypass of tenant quota or tenant->dedicated routing. header = preference only. console should show effective evaluated chain.

chris: implementation notes: router evaluates in this order: 1) route-level fallback_chain if present 2) tenant soft-preference (X-RI-Fallback-Priority) merged into chain 3) global policy lanes (cost/latency tiers). must atomically compute chain before capacity checks to avoid ABA.

alex: also want a preemptive-shed stage: if pool_util > 0.9 then cut requests to reduced-context early instead of waiting for cb. i.e. capacity-shedding rule precedes cb open.

sam: +1. cb opens too late for tail latency. preemptive shed gives graceful degradation. set preemptive threshold to 0.85 for now.

chris: telemetry additions: emit routing.eval_chain (list), routing.reason (cb_open | preemptive_shed | explicit_fallback), routing.cb_window_ms, and metrics for fallback_transition_count. also record which model version used (to compare quality/regressions).

maria: UI/rollout UX: add a toggle in console Rollouts to switch between "strict priority" and "soft merge" for tenant header merging so we can A/B test behavior. show preview of evaluated chain before applying.

alex: code snippet for route yaml i mocked: 
```yaml
routes:
  - path: /v1/generate
    model: redwood-13b
    fallback_chain: [redwood-13b-rc, redwood-13b-compress, redwood-7b-backup]
    preemptive_shed_threshold: 0.85
    cb_policy:
      latency_p95_ms: 2000
      error_rate: 0.12
      cool_down_sec: 30
```

chris: small nit: use ms for latency fields and decimal for error_rate. also cb cool_down should be configurable per-tenant for enterprise.

sam: alerting changes: add alert when fallback_transition_count spikes > 10/min for a tenant, and when routing.reason == cb_open and pool_util > 0.95. connect to oncall playbook.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: feature/route-fallback-chain -> staging. dry-run flag enabled.

maria: before we deploy to staging, let's run a chaos test: simulate 3x load on a single GPU pool and verify chain behavior + telemetry. also add an eval to ensure fallback models don't regress quality beyond 3% prompt-rouge on our production prompt set.

alex: I'll add the chaos test harness and a prom query dashboard. can someone add the console preview mock?

chris: I'll wire telemetry and the preview. keeping header advisory logic in gateway layer.

sam: I'll update oncall runbook and add pager rule for fallback_transition_count.

observability-bot: note: new metrics created: routing_eval_chain (labelled), fallback_transition_count, preemptive_shedding_events, cb_open_events. metrics will roll out after staging deploy.

alex: perfect. plan: merge -> staging dry-run -> chaos + quality eval -> prod rollout with canary for 10% traffic. document the new fields in API spec.

maria: +1. anyone opposed to default preemptive threshold 0.85?

chris: fine by me. we'll make it overrideable per-route.

sam: fine from SRE side as long as we have alerts.

alex: ok locking it in. i'll open a follow-up thread for console copy/UX details. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
